body: As part of the Oru Pid Ari Project to collect a fistful of rice from each child . The students of the school jointly collected 140 kg of rice which was handed over to Asha Bhavan.The visit made the students aware of the need to support the unprivileged people.

On 22nd August 2019 Students of our Vidyalaya distributed relief materials to the victims of flood, residing at Kuttur, Thrissur District in the presence of Sri Unnikrishnan Panchayath President Kolazhy, Smt Shoba Menon Principal and Smt Usha Prem Vice Principal. A kit containing various articles was distributed and the benevolence shown by our students from class 1 to class XII was invigorating and appreciable. Oru Pidi Ari - ( A Fistful of rice) By the Tiny Tots- 70 Kg of Rice to Asha Bhavan

It was decided that the students would pool money and distribute ONAM kits to 40 different poor families These kits included all the necessary items for them to have a sumptuous meal. Students had identified 40 families in keeping with the RUBY JUBIlEE CELBRATIONS of the Vidyalaya

Kuttanad in Alleppy district of Kerala was the worst and earliest affected in flood ravaged Kerala. Students of Chinmaya Vidyalaya have empathized and contributed substantially to a relief project intitated by the daily Mathrubhumi-'A supporting Hand to Kuttandu' contributing essential items like bedsheets, towels, soaps, Dettol bleaching powder, biscuits, pulses, candles etc.
Donated 300 books to Ramavarmapuram Government Schools on 13.11.2017 Class 12th students donated study materials like books,pens etc to NSS Boys hostel on 14.11.17

Class 11 along with their teachers embarked on a social service venture by distributing lunch food packets to the needy as part of Gurupurnima Celebrations. The zest and zeal of students to "Share" and "Care" for the people who battle for survival is incredible. By being generous in the service of the community, the students decipher the meaning of life. The children wholeheartedly foray into the world of communal service and to salvage this spirit, our school has initiated myriad programmes to strengthen this "bond".

Students of Class 9 celebrated Christmas in a different way. They visited the differently abled children at Reach Swasraya and entertained them. Each child carried a gift for one of the inmates of the organization.
As part of the 'Oru Pidi Ari' inititative 50Kgs of rice was collected from classes 3 to 6 and this was donated to Asha Orphanage , Ramavarmapuram on 20th February 2017.

body: The students of our Vidyalaya visited a Tribal Colony in Wynad to hand over medicines, clothes and money. The money would be utilized to construct a well, the group had an interaction with the tribal elders and children and could gain an idea of their way of life. The students contributed willingly to purchase iron tablets, which were supplied to the tribal women of Attappady, where poverty is endemic. Responding positively towards the appeal made by Sri.Vijay Menon during his talk on 15-6-2015 students of 11th Std. generously contributed an amount of Rs.14,595/- for buying sleeping mats for the Tribals of Wyanad District. These mats were handed over to the representatives.

Our school extended a helping hand to the Chennai's rain affected citizens. Understanding the immediate requirements of the rain ravaged citizens of Chennai, the young children responded clarion call of the needy proving the fact that compassion and generosity still prevail in their heart.

"Service With A Smile" is the holy mantra which we voice and value - to decorate our life with joy by serving with a smile for someone who is in need. Children willingly drop money into the donation box kept in the school portico which is channelized for the needy.
"One Rupee, One Life" Scheme was embraced by our student community. It encourages each child to contribute one rupee from their pocket money to be used for Palliative Care."

A day of fulfillment for the students of Class IX. Once a year, the students of Std. IX visit Swasraya Reach Us and try to illuminate the dampened spirits and bring joy to the lives of the differently abled children there by befriending them and bestowing gifts upon them.

title: Investiture Ceremony

body: The Investiture Ceremony at Chinmaya Vidyalaya, Kolazhy, Thrissur on 27th July 2023 was a momentous occasion filled with pride and honour. The ceremony was graced by the presence of the esteemed Chief Guest, IPS Aiswarya Dongre, Rural SP, H H Swami Gabeeranandaji, Acharya, Chinmaya Mission Thrissur, Director of Education Dr V Venugopal, Principal Smt. Usha Kumari P, Vice Principal Smt Latha E T, Sr. Headmistress Smt. Bindu K and Headmaster Sri Madhavdasan K. In her inaugural address, IPS Aishwarya Dongre emphasized the importance of leadership and urged the students to embrace their roles with passion and empathy. Her inspiring words resonated with the audience, leaving them motivated and inspired to achieve greatness.

The newly appointed Office Bearers then took a solemn pledge, vowing to carry out their duties with utmost sincerity and to uphold the values of the school. In conclusion, the Investiture Ceremony at Chinmaya Vidyalaya was a remarkable event that marked the beginning of a transformative leadership journey for the newly appointed Office Bearers. With the guidance and support of the school, they are poised to make a positive impact and bring about positive change within the school and beyond. .

body: The Navaratri celebration of the Vidyalaya was a dance and musical extravaganza. Classical dances and music, instrumental music, bhajans and various cultural programmes added glory to the talents of the children. The two dance teachers of our Vidyalaya also presented a solo dance.

In connection with National Ayurveda Day Celebrations, Dhanvantharai Jayanthi was observed on 28th October 2016 by Ayurveda Medical Officers Association. A curtain raiser of this programme was held in our Vidyalaya on 27th Oct.2016.The programme started with prayer followed by welcome address by Vice Principal and felicitation by Dr. G Mukundan ,Director of Education. An introduction through power point presentation on 'Healthy life style and life style diseases' was given by medical officers. A quiz competition was also held in the Vidyalaya on the' Role of plants as drugs and diet'.

Kerala Piravi was celebrated in the Vidyalaya with enthralling programmes perfomed by children on 1st November 2016. A few children recited poems in Malayalam which was an audio feast on this apt day. A map of Kerala state was displayed in which each district was decorated with different pulses and grains. .A debate on the 'Changing Culture of Kerala' was conducted by students. ONV Krupp's famous poem 'AMMA' was enacted in a typical Kerala dance form which was a feast to the eye and ear. Three non teaching staff of the Vidyalaya ,Sri Mohanan ,Sri Ayappan and ,Sri Krishnadas were felicitated on this occasion by Director of Education Dr. G Mukundan in the presence of Principal, Vice Principal and Head mistress.

Children's day celebration,held on 14th November 2016,was hosted by the teachers of the Vidyalaya. Poetry in motion show was organized by the teachers of the Malayalam department. Children - Our wealth and treasure" was a presentation where the teachers enacted different characters exhibited by children over years. Characters like smart, lazy, glutton, punctual, happy- goâ€“lucky, eloquent, loner, book worm, nerd, pranksters, latecomer's etc. showcased themselves with suitable narration. The presentation received tremendous appreciation from the children.

The Chinmaya Birth Centenary celebrations grand finale was held in the Chinmaya Janmashathabdi Nagar near Neeranjali hall on the 21st and the 22nd May. The Chief Guest of the day was Justice A Hari Prasad of the Kerala High Court. Padmasree P. R. Krishnakumar, chancellor, Avinasalingam University was a special guest. Adv. Therambil Ramakrishnan offered felicitations. Dr. G.Mukundan, Director of Education, Chinmaya Vidyalaya and Chief Sevak, Chinmaya Seva Trust, Kerala, presented mementos to the dignitaries. Sri .P. Krishnakumar, General Convener, welcomed the gathering and Sri T.M Reghunandan, Treasurer, Chinmaya Seva Trust, Kerala offered the vote of thanks. Eminent speakers like Swami Chidanandapuri, Sri Gopalakrishnan Vaidik, Sri Rahul Easwer, Sri Vijaya Menon etc. to name a few graced the occasion. The valedictory function was on 22nd May, the Chief Guest being Padmasree Dr. Sunder Menon. Acharyas, Chief Sevaks and all the teachers behind the cultural programmes were honoured.

title: National Energy Conservation

body: December 14th is National Energy Conservation. The day began with an awareness talk on conserving energy and followed by the students of entire school pledging to conserve energy. This was followed by a slogan writing competition. The entire school expressed their concern and solidarity by switching off all lights and fans for nearly one and half hours. An energy audit was carried out by the Eco club members to create awareness about energy consumption in the Vidyalaya. The Centenary year of Cubs and Bulbul was observed in the Vidyalaya. She won the TCS best student award of 2015 batch among all disciplines of GEC Thrissur ,Kerala.

body: "Haritha Keralam" an initiative by the state govt. was launched statewide on 8th December 2016. This programme basically deals with two aspects- Water Conservation and Water Management. Our Vidyalaya organized an awareness programme as a part of this. The students went around the neighborhood spreading the message of green and clean Kerala. To instil the value of conserving water, every child was made to spill out their extra water in to a bucket, at the end of school hours. This act was highly self motivating.

World Gita day was observed on 10th December 2016. This year it was decided to organize The Global Gita chanting programme. 18 selected slokas from Gita was chanted by the student and teachers in our vidyalaya. The whole atmosphere was reverberated with the chanting of slokas.

title: World Environment Day

body: The day was observed in the Vidyalaya on June 6th. Our honorable Chief Guest Smt. Jalaja S. Menon, Assistant Professor, Kerala Agricultural University addressed the students emphasizing the need to conserve soil and to protect wildlife. She was presented with a memento comprising of a paper bag, seeds, and vermicompost packet and sandal wood sapling. A poster making competition along with a Rangoli competition was held and the winners were presented with ginger saplings. The assembly ended with a pledge to protect the environment.

An awareness programme on 'Together for road safety' was held in the Vidyalaya on 19th July. It was a joint venture of Malayala Manorama and Credai builders, Thrissur. Vice Principal, Smt. Shobha Menon, welcomed the gathering and introduced the guest. The session was presided by Psy. Vipin V Roldant, Consultant, Psychologist and Performance Coach, Sunrise Hospital, Cochin. It was an interactive session on the importance of following traffic rules for the safety of the driver as well as the pedestrians. He explained the facts leading to accidents from the psychological point of view. Mr. M Nandakumar, Circulation Inspector, Malayala Manorama, Thrissur proposed the vote of thanks.

title: Reception of Chinmaya Jyoti

body: Chinmaya Jyothi which was lit on May 8 at Ernakulam by H.H.Swami Tejomayananda to mark the launch of CBCC reached the Vidyalaya in the Chinmaya vahini along with the paduka, vastra and the coin released by the Prime Minister of India, at 12 noon. The Jyoti was received from Br. Mukunda Chaitanya with a poorna kumbham by the Director of Education, Dr. G.Mukundan. The Principal, Vice Principal and Head Mistress paid their tribute to the other three sacred objects by garlanding them.

title: Adolescence education / sex education of 11

body: A talk on adolescent education/ sex education for standard 11th girls and boys was organised separately on 16th November 2019 Saturday in the conference call and Chinmaya Balkrishnana respectively. The talk focused on their right to know about themselves, their adolescence and their sexuality basic facts on HIV and other ST's develop and reinforce life skills that enable them to protect themselves dispel myths and clarify misconceptions and so on. title: Samanvayam

body: The annual Fun, Food and games Carnival "Samanvayam was held in the Vidyalaya on 29 th January 2019. There are food items which can tickle anyones taste buds and also a member of innovative and fun filled games that literally take your breath away.

Another talk was conducted exclusively for the students of the commerce stream by Sri M Satyakumar on the topic Designing Career, Transforming India. He discussed in simple language the dilemma in opting for a subject for and after the plus two level and the plethora of opportunities available for commerce graduates. He was able to create a good rapport with the students and received great appreciation from them. Sri C K Suresh of ATMA Foundation addressed the students of class XI and XII on 9th October 2018. Sir spoke about the factors necessary to reach ones goal. He associated the factors essential for success with the word COAT- Curiosity, Openness, Alertness and Thoughtfulness. Sir insisted that succeeding in a changing world is beyond just survival and inspired children for a life of self-empowerment through enthusiasm, energy, emotional well â€“being and efficiency. Students of classes XI and XII were fortunate to be addressed by H H Swami Adwayanda on 6th July 2018 on the topic 'Key to a Happy and Successful life'. It was a refreshing and recharging session where Swamiji defined and commented on success through short stories which were appealing, motivating and edifying.
